question.text: Priya, age 17, has mutual fund investments made by her father as guardian. She turns 18 next month. What happens to her SIP if no action is taken?

answer.text: The SIP continues normally as her father remains the guardian
The SIP amount doubles since she is now an adult

The SIP and other standing instructions (such as STP and SWP), along with customer-initiated transactions, will be suspended/frozen until the minor-to-major (MAM) status change is completed with fresh KYC and updated bank/signature details
The SIP will be automatically transferred to her father's account

explanation.text: The Logic: When a minor turns 18, the guardian's authority to operate the account ceases. SIP and other standing instructions (SIP, STP, SWP) are suspended, and customer-initiated transactions cannot be processed until the minor-to-major (MAM) status change is completed — fresh KYC in her own name, status change from minor to major, and updated bank/signature/contact details. The Trap: Saying "all transactions" is overbroad — IDCW payout/reinvestment may continue under the existing instruction even while standing instructions and customer-initiated transactions are frozen. The freeze is not automatic in the sense of self-correcting; the investor/guardian must complete the MAM process. Note: Source: NISM Series V-A (Mutual Fund Distributors) workbook, pp.215-217 — minor-to-major status change suspends SIP/STP/SWP and customer-initiated transactions until documents/KYC/status change are completed; IDCW continuation noted.
